newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-1860 LODGE COMPLAINT AGAINST KARLSRUHE DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-1860 LODGE COMPLAINT AGAINST KARLSRUHE DRAW.

text.p: German first division side 1860 Munich on Thursday lodged a complaint with the German soccer federation (DFB) over a referee's decision which cost them a win over Karlsruhe on Tuesday.

The Munich side were leading 2-1 until the 87th minute when Germany striker Sean Dundee equalised for Karlsruhe. But 1860 say Dundee's goal came after referee Michael Marlbranc blew for a foul on Karlsruhe's Thomas Haessler.
Marlbranc denied he blew his whistle, although Haessler said he thought the referee had given him a free kick.
"I thought he had given a free kick. But what could we do? Then we were all celebrating anyway," Haessler said after the game.
The 2-2 draw kept Karlsruhe with the Bundesliga leaders in third place, while unlucky 1860 is languishing in 13th place.
1860 studied television pictures of the game, but none show whether Malbranc had the whistle in his mouth at the moment in question, although a whistle sounding is clearly audible.
German rules state a side can make an official complaint within 48 hours of the game in question if "a rule violation by the referee very probably influenced the outcome of the game".
If the DFB rules that Marlbranc made a mistake the match will have to be replayed.
